nodes.summary: A binary code of length $n$ is a linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, the vector space of words of length $n$ over the two-element field $\mathbb{F}_2$.
nodes.title: Binary code

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $q$, this is the collection of all subsets $S \subseteq \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ with at most $q$ elements.
nodes.title: Subsets with at most $q$ elements

nodes.summary: The dimension of a binary code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is its dimension as a vector space over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
nodes.title: Dimension of a binary code

nodes.summary: For a binary code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ and a word $f \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the distance from $f$ to $C$ is the minimum, over all codewords $c \in C$, of the Hamming distance between $f$ and $c$, that is, the number of coordinates in which $f$ and $c$ differ.
nodes.title: Distance from a word to a binary code

nodes.summary: The distance of a binary code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is the smallest Hamming weight (number of nonzero coordinates) of a nonzero codeword of $C$, and is $0$ if $C = \{0\}$.
nodes.title: Minimum distance of a binary code

nodes.summary: Let $(n_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be natural numbers and, for each $i$, let $C_i \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^{n_i}$ be a binary code of length $n_i$. The family $(C_i)$ is good if $n_i \to \infty$ as $i \to \infty$ and there is a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every $i$ both the rate and the normalised distance of $C_i$ are at least $\varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Good family of codes

nodes.summary: Let $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a binary code, let $q$ be a natural number and let $\kappa \ge 0$ be a real number. A $\kappa$-local tester for $C$ with $q$ queries consists of a probability distribution on the subsets $S \subseteq \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ with at most $q$ elements, together with, for each such $S$, a set $V_S \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^S$ of allowed local views, such that: at least $\kappa$ times…
nodes.title: Locally testable code

nodes.summary: For a binary code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ and a word $f \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the normalised distance from $f$ to $C$ is the distance from $f$ to $C$ (the Hamming distance from $f$ to a closest codeword) divided by the length $n$, as a nonnegative real number; it is $0$ when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Normalised distance from a word to a binary code

nodes.summary: The normalised distance of a binary code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is its distance divided by its length $n$, as a real number; it is $0$ when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Normalised distance of a binary code

nodes.summary: The rate of a binary code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is its dimension over $\mathbb{F}_2$ divided by its length $n$, as a real number; it is $0$ when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Rate of a binary code

nodes.summary: For every real number $\rho$ with $0 \le \rho < 1$ there exist a natural number $q$, a real number $\kappa > 0$, lengths $n_i \in \mathbb{N}$ and binary codes $C_i$ of length $n_i$ for $i \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the family $(C_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ is good and, for every $i$, the code $C_i$ is $\kappa$-locally testable with $q$ queries and has rate at least $\rho$.
nodes.title: Good locally testable codes of every rate below one

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
